title: Temporal Experience
relevance: Canonical reconstruction of the antireductionist argument from experience to nowness and passage; her reductionist reply is the load-bearing objection for this repo's deflationary moves
limits: Author copy; roughly the first half read (pp. 333-338 and the argument reconstruction); her apparent-motion discussion and later sections not fully read
version: Journal of Philosophy CVII(7), July 2010, 333-359; author copy at lapaul.org
locator: argument (1)-(5) at pp. 337-338; defenders catalogued with footnotes 5-10 (Williams, Craig, Schlesinger, Broad 1938, Smith, Maudlin, Skow, Hare)
assumptions: experiences as of nowness/passage exist (assumed, not argued); IBE methodology
conclusion: the antireductionist route from experience to nowness/passage is blocked if the reductionist explains the experiences; her paper supplies such an explanation and shifts the burden
dependencies: Mellor Real Time II; Williams 1951; experimental work on apparent motion
open_questions: does her positive reductionist account survive Prosser's stronger claim that passage-content is unrepresentable?

title: The Temporal Structure of Experience
relevance: The 'naive view' and the rejection of the principle of simultaneous awareness; restructures the whole retentional/extensional/cinematic debate
limits: author copy via JSTOR scan; roughly first third read (7.1-7.3); postdiction sections not read
version: in V. Arstila, D. Lloyd (eds.), Subjective Time: The Philosophy, Psychology, and Neuroscience of Temporality, MIT Press 2014, ch. 7; JSTOR j.ctt9qf5dd.14
locator: 7.1 Overview; 7.2 The Traditional Problematic (PSA from Miller 1984: 109; Reid 1827: 387; Prichard 1950: 47; Le Poidevin 2007: 92, 99; Gallistel 1996: 336); Kelly 2005: 210 quoted in 7.3
assumptions: PSA is false (taken from his earlier work); temporal properties are the only properties manifestly shared by objects of experience and experience itself
conclusion: streams of consciousness inherit the temporal structure of their objects when all goes well; the traditional problematics are unnecessary once PSA is dropped
open_questions: does the naive view handle postdictive phenomena (his claimed empirical objection target)?
doi: none (JSTOR stable URL j.ctt9qf5dd.14 recorded in version)

title: Rethinking the Specious Present
relevance: Supplies the standard taxonomy (retentional/extensional/cinematic) with defender lists, the Broad motion quote with exact page, and the dynamic snapshot theory; backbone of READING.md section 1
limits: open-access repository copy; roughly first half read (through the start of the dynamic snapshot theory); the discontinuous-change account not read
version: Routledge eBook chapter, published 2017-09-19; St Andrews repository OA copy
locator: Introduction; The Current Orthodoxy (retentional: Broad 1938, Lee 2014; extensional: Foster, Dainton, Hoerl, Phillips, Rashbrook; cinematic: Chuard 2011); Arguments for the Specious Present (Broad 1923: 351 quoted)
assumptions: experience has instantaneous content with finite resolution; a problematic Cartesian assumption underlies current debate
conclusion: every current version of the specious-present doctrine should be rejected; replaced by a dynamic snapshot theory for continuous change plus a separate account for discontinuous change
open_questions: the account of discontinuous change (unread); whether finite resolution survives the resolution/content-instant distinction

title: Explaining away temporal flow - thoughts on Prosser's Experiencing Time
relevance: Defines Perceptualism; the main published challenge to Prosser's mechanism, directly bearing on the special question (no argument from experience needs a primitive present)
limits: philpapers copy; abstract, introduction and the perceptual-evidence section read; later sections on rate of passage and movement not read
locator: abstract; Introduction; 'Do we have perceptual evidence for strong passage?'
assumptions: Perceptualism = experience represents strong passage and gives evidence for it
conclusion: accepts that perception gives no experiential justification for the A-theory, but Prosser's perceptual-sensitivity argument over-generalizes (spatial-world knowledge) and needs theory/observation constraints he does not supply
open_questions: what conditions on the theory/observation distinction would finish the argument?

title: Experience, Thought, and the Metaphysics of Time
relevance: The no-representation-of-A-properties argument in accessible form; core of the deflationary position
limits: philpapers copy; introduction and A/B framing read (roughly first quarter); the argument proper partially read
version: in K. Jaszczolt, L. de Saussure (eds.), Time: Language, Cognition and Reality, OUP 2013, 157-174 (web version 2014)
conclusion: there can be no mental representation of objective tensed features, whether or not they exist; so no semantics should treat A-properties as semantic values
open_questions: whether the argument extends from perception to thought as claimed

title: The Perception of Time (Principles of Psychology, ch. XV)
relevance: Primary historical source: the specious present enters Anglophone philosophy here; verifies Clay's coinage and James's stream doctrine
limits: online text of the 1890 edition; opening portion read (pp. 605-609 area), not the whole chapter
version: The Principles of Psychology, 1890, ch. XV; psychclassics.yorku.ca transcription
locator: opening pages: 'constant feeling sui generis of pastness'; E. R. Clay's 'specious present' quoted at pp. 608-609; pages 606-609 seen directly
assumptions: consciousness is not a string of bead-like sensations
conclusion: the sensible present has duration; the specious present is the prototype of all conceived times
open_questions: the rest of the chapter (Exner/Helmholtz/Wundt experiments)
dependencies: nineteenth-century German psychophysics discussed in the chapter (Exner, Helmholtz, Wundt)

title: Thank Goodness That's Over
relevance: Primary source of the tensed-attitude argument; the 'presence of experience' family's rational-attitudes route
limits: Cambridge Core open PDF; the whole paper read at fetch depth; targets N. L. Wilson's substance-language, so the thank-goodness passage is embedded in a technical polemic
locator: the thank-goodness passage at p. 17: not equivalent to dated tenseless proposition nor to contemporaneity-with-utterance; 'having been green in August' analysis earlier in the paper
assumptions: tensed copula is primitive; substance-language needs tenses
conclusion: no tenseless-copula-plus-date analysis conveys the tensed attitude
dependencies: Wilson 1955/1956; Geach's 1957 criticism (acknowledged in the paper)
open_questions: whether the argument survives the indexical/de se reply
